name: Sprocket
text: Add a mandatory prompt review step at the start of every task. This forces us to verify the prompt’s clarity, scope, and constraints before execution, cutting wasted work from misaligned inputs. The trade-off is a small upfront time cost, but it prevents larger rework later. Without this, we risk solving the wrong problem or missing critical constraints.

name: Gauge
text: Mandatory prompt review risks review fatigue where reviewers gloss over prompts after the 10th task, turning a safeguard into a checkbox. Instead, automate a lightweight pre-check that flags only high-risk prompts (e.g., vague scope, missing constraints) for human review—this cuts wasted work without creating a new bottleneck. Settle this by running a 2-week pilot: compare rework rates and reviewer satisfaction with and without the automation.

name: Sprocket
text:
Do this: Run a weekly automated scan of all prompts in our system, flagging any that lack clear success criteria or constraints. Flagged prompts go to a human for review before execution.

This cuts wasted work by catching misaligned inputs early without slowing every task with a full review. The trade-off is missing edge cases that don’t match our flagging rules—but the weekly cadence balances speed and safety better than a mandatory step for every prompt.

name: Gauge
text: Gauge: A weekly scan misses urgent misalignments—vague prompts in fast-moving tasks slip through until the next scan, wasting work now. Instead, tie the pre-check to *task initiation*: auto-flag prompts with missing success criteria or constraints at the moment they’re created, forcing human review *before* execution starts. Settle it by testing both: measure wasted work from misaligned prompts in the next 2 weeks with the weekly scan, then the same period with the real-time flagging.
